clue.text: Film star no more, tragically

indicators.note: things going tragically go badly wrong, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lament that a famous screen actor has died, a sad loss to the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tragically' rearranges NOMORE. The surface nods to Marilyn Monroe's early death.
explanation.definitionFit: Marilyn Monroe was one of the most famous Hollywood actresses of the 1950s.

clue.text: Nice houses builders produced covering island

indicators.note: the builders wrap round the island letter

parts.note: masons are stone builders

explanation.surface: Builders put up lovely homes on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the French city, so the houses are French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for dwellings, as used in the city on the Riviera.

clue.text: Desert, for example, in largely arid state

indicators.note: the example abbreviation goes inside
only the larger part of the state's name is kept, its first half

parts.note: Nevada is a dry US state

explanation.surface: A desert, say, found in a mostly dry state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' keeps the bigger half of the state's name, NEV. The surface wants Nevada's own desert, but the answer lies in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Negev is the large arid region of southern Israel.

clue.text: Mated with variation, exposed without bishop and queen

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word goes round the others

parts.note: outed means exposed publicly
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
R is for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A chess game ends in mate, the bishop and queen left exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, so OUTED surrounds B and R. Chess terms mislead: mated means bred.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed with unrelated stock introduces variety, the opposite of inbreeding.

clue.text: A king badly hurt at the end

definitions.text: A king badly hurt at the end

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex), as on chess notation

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch receives a fatal wound in his final battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' gives THUR, placed at the end. The whole clue also tells the legend: the king was mortally wounded at Camlann, his last fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary British monarch of the Round Table was fatally wounded at his last battle, so the whole clue describes him.

clue.text: Again try to get male parent outside

indicators.note: the parent word sits outside the male one

parts.note: to rear is to raise children, to parent
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone attempts once more to get a father out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the parent word round the male one. Try is the courtroom sense, not an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear a case afresh in court is to try it a second time.

clue.text: Two chaps with ecstasy, one preferring grass

parts.note: Herb is a man's name, the first of two
Ivor is another man's name, the second chap
E is the street name for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A pair of men on drugs, one of whom favours cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass looks like the drug, given the ecstasy, but it is real grass that is eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant-eating animal, such as a cow, feeds on vegetation like grass.

clue.text: Put in new position, took a break around one

indicators.note: the resting word goes around the numeral

parts.note: rested means paused for a break
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A worker moved to a new spot pauses around one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts RESTED round I.
explanation.definitionFit: To relocate a building or object is to place it at another site.

clue.text: Treat Texan who lived in the margins here, noted literary figure

parts.note: to doctor is to give medical treatment

parts.words: Texan who lived in the margins here
parts.note: Lyndon B Johnson, the Texan president; the presidents in this puzzle sit around the grid's edges

explanation.surface: A literary celebrity treated a Texan living on the fringes.
explanation.walkthrough: The margins are the grid's edges, where this puzzle's US presidents (MONROE, ARTHUR, HOOVER and others) are entered; the Texan is Lyndon Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Johnson, compiler of the famous eighteenth-century dictionary, is widely known by this title.

clue.text: Injure player on side

definitions.meaning: a forward who plays on the flank of a football or hockey team

explanation.surface: Someone hurts a team-mate.
explanation.definitionFit: To wound a bird in flight is to clip it in the arm-like limb; a winger plays on the flank.

clue.text: It's as well flier has concealed British kind of moustache

parts.note: as well means too, in addition

indicators.note: the bird's name hides a letter inside it, so it is cut open for one

parts.note: a thrush is a songbird, something that flies

explanation.surface: A bird with something British hidden on it, resembling a small clipped moustache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has concealed' puts the British letter inside the bird. The kind of moustache is the short bristly one named after a bathroom brush.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, bristly moustache is named for its resemblance to the bristles of a cleaning implement for teeth.

clue.text: Clean house again

parts.note: over means again, as in doing something over

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy the home once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also a US president, the puzzle's hidden theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacuum a carpet, from the brand-name machine used for the job.

clue.text: Unusually irate, not otherwise disposed to attack

indicators.note: letters arranged in an unusual way are not in their normal order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone, though angry, is not otherwise inclined to violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges IRATENOT; 'otherwise disposed to' only links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch into a fierce assault, physical or verbal, on someone.

clue.text: Population of Ireland, say, is riven by malicious gossip

indicators.note: the word is is split apart so the gossip can fit between its letters

parts.note: taken as written
slander is damaging, malicious talk

explanation.surface: A nation divided by spiteful rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riven by' splits the little word apart around the gossip. Ireland, say, flags an example: its people are island dwellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is an island, so its people are an example of those who live on islands.

clue.text: They provide pardons, for instance, covering me, initially, then you

indicators.note: the outer word wraps round the pieces that follow

parts.note: as means for instance, as in 'animals, as dogs'
me is the setter, Brendan, whose initial is B
you, reading the puzzle, are the solver

explanation.surface: A priest or official forgives, say, me first and then you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts B and SOLVER inside AS. 'me' is the setter Brendan and 'you' the solver, a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who grant forgiveness or release from guilt, such as priests at confession.

clue.text: Supporting diamonds as bridge alternative

parts.note: for means in favour of, supporting
D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player backs a diamond bid as an option in the game of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge is not the card game but a structure over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow crossing place where a river can be waded is the way across when there is no span over it.

clue.text: Travel, in a way, hard in wild terrain

parts.note: to bus is to travel by one form of road transport
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Journeying across rugged, untamed country is tough going.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncultivated scrubland, especially in Australia or Africa, is called by this name.

clue.text: Lawyers' test to expose greatest upset

parts.note: to bare is to uncover or expose

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: max is short for maximum, the greatest

explanation.surface: An exam for lawyers designed to reveal who is best, unsettlingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MAX into XAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The US examination that law graduates must pass to be admitted to practise.

clue.text: A letter or two, so to speak

definitions.meaning: the name of the twenty-third letter of the alphabet
said loosely, a pair of the person addressed, twice the reader

explanation.surface: A note written to one or two people.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter W is named as a doubled U, and the same sounds can mean two of the person addressed.

clue.text: Rely on capital from Asia to produce growth in Australia

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on, so bank stands for it

indicators.note: the capital, the initial A, is taken from the continent's name

explanation.surface: Depending on money from Asia to build an economy in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital from' removes the initial A of Asia, leaving SIA. Capital and growth suggest finance, but growth is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Banksias are Australian shrubs and trees with bottlebrush flowers, named for Sir Joseph Banks.

clue.text: Moderate losing head with ruler on more occasions

indicators.note: the word drops its first letter

parts.note: to soften is to moderate
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A moderate politician loses his leader to a monarch repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' removes S from SOFTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative of frequently: happening more frequently than before.

clue.text: Former Labour leader slow in changing

indicators.note: letters that are changing shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A past Labour leader was slow to embrace change.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is the British left-wing party; Harold Wilson led it and was Prime Minister in the 1960s and 70s. It is also a US president, the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Wilson led the British Labour Party and was twice Prime Minister.

clue.text: Continue singing, including one great number

indicators.note: the phrase takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: to trill on is to keep warbling
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A singer carries on with a big song number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' takes the numeral inside. Number looks like a song, keeping the singing theme, but it is a quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A million million is a huge figure; the clue's number is a quantity, not a song.

clue.text: Men on board announced times for retirement

indicators.note: said out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: chess pieces are called men, and the knights are among them

explanation.surface: Crew members on a ship are told when they can leave work for good.
explanation.walkthrough: The board is a chessboard and retirement is going to bed, not leaving a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring here means going to bed, which people do in the hours of darkness.

clue.text: Gift from relative coming on time

indicators.note: in a down clue the time letter comes on, after, the relative

parts.note: gran is grandmother, a relative

explanation.surface: A present from a relative arrives on time.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum of money awarded, such as for study, is a donation.

clue.text: Results from adding six one's incorrectly divided by x

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are split apart with another piece placed between them
letters set down incorrectly are out of their proper order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters of six and ones
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: An arithmetic slip: dividing a sum by x gives the wrong answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrectly' gives EXSIONS, and 'divided by' splits it round the Roman ten. The arithmetic reading of divided is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Additions built onto a house or a deadline are the things that result from adding.

clue.text: Arranger, oddly enough, a regular Prom contributor

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: Strangely, a music arranger is a frequent performer at the summer concerts.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a London summer concert series; Thomas Arne's Rule, Britannia! is sung every Last Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth-century English composer's patriotic song is a fixture at the Proms each year.

clue.text: In front of mirror, taking advantage of reflection

indicators.note: the front of the word mirror is its opening letter

parts.note: using means exploiting, taking advantage of

explanation.surface: Someone gazing into a looking glass and making the most of their reflected image.
explanation.walkthrough: The mirror's reflection is a red herring: the definition means thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiet contemplation or pondering is another word for reflection in its thinking sense.

clue.text: Driver's temperature taken by nurse, say

definitions.note: read as 'driver is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: the temperature is taken in by the carer, placed inside her

parts.note: a nurse is an example of a carer

explanation.surface: A nurse takes a chauffeur's temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' puts T inside CARER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who drives a horse-drawn cart for a living was named for the vehicle.
